newsitem.title: USA: Canadian lt. crude cargo resold to Shell - traders.
newsitem.headline: Canadian lt. crude cargo resold to Shell - traders.

text.p: A cargo of Koch Alberta crude destined for Chevron Corp in California was resold to Shell Oil Co this week, traders said on Friday.
"There was a cargo of Koch Alberta destined for (Chevron) that went to Shell," a source familiar with the deal said.
The cargo contains 500,000 barrels of the light crude, which has a 33 degree API gravity and one percent sulphur content.
The grade is often a substitute for the region's benchmark Alaska North Slope (ANS) grade.
Traders said the cargo was tendered to Chevron in December and is loading this week.
Astra Oil Co, a unit of the Argentine energy company Astra CAPSA, originally sold the cargo to Chevron.
Another trader said "perceived quality problems" prompted the resale to Shell.
